additional_info.subject: RE: ID0472758-DC/Si-D/AT- [Y2/T3314161484002] Intermittent Bender BUS Communication Failure CRM:03276000034
additional_info.body:
Hello Felipe,
as mentioned in the ticket, this error occurs only after a restart. After that, a large number of additional restarts are required until the error disappears again.
As also stated, I have already inspected the entire cabling, as I initially suspected a loose connection. However, nothing abnormal could be found.
I opened the ticket because I am out of ideas at this point. Is this an isolated case, or does this issue also occur with other chargers? Are there any known experiences or reference cases?
What would you recommend as the next step? My next step would be to replace the SECC.
During the last three service visits (which were originally for other issues), this error appeared again. For example: I travel to the site to replace a converter, replace the converter, and then additionally spend around three hours troubleshooting the IMD fault.
BR
Daniel

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0472758-DC/Si-D/AT- [Y2/T3314161484002] Intermittent Bender BUS Communication Failure CRM:03289000274
additional_info.body:
Hi Felipe,
no, this only happens after a restart. As a result, the station goes into a fault state and no charging session can be started. The error sometimes clears after a few restarts, but it keeps reappearing.
As mentioned, I would normally suspect a loose connection if a Modbus communication issue occurs after rebooting. However, I have already disassembled and reassembled the entire wiring.
Therefore, I can only assume that either the controller is defective or one of the IMDs has a fault and is disrupting communication with the others.
I’m currently on my way to the customer again due to another issue with a different charger. If I have time afterwards, I can get in touch with you via Teams and we can take a look at it together on-site.
BR
Daniel
